preamble: Assimilation of the coda tap [ɾ] to a following glottal fricative, giving a voiced [ɦ] before [h]: [ɦh]. In western Cuban Spanish (the provinces from Pinar del Río to Matanzas and Cienfuegos, including Havana, plus the municipalities of Corralillo and Trinidad), coda /ɾ/ and coda /l/ merge and assimilate to the next consonant. Before /h/ (spelled j, or g before e and i) the merged liquid takes the glottal place of the following consonant and keeps its voicing at first, so virgen is pronounced vi[ɦh]en. Guitart (1978, 2004) also describes the first element as voiced; Costa Sánchez (1984) reports voicing of the whole sequence, which he writes [ʜʜ], and for central Cuba (1987a) lengthening of the preceding vowel instead (all as summarized by Arias 2019). Arias assigns [ɦ] to the phoneme /h/, not to the merged liquid. The unassimilated pronunciations remain more common.
phoneticEffects: Regressive Assimilation, Place Assimilation, Debuccalization, Gemination

examples.note: Arias doubts that it contrasts with sacas gente, saca[hh]ente.

sources: Arias Cabal, Á. (2019). Fonética y fonología de las consonantes geminadas en el español de Cuba. Moenia, 25, 465–497. https://revistas.usc.gal/index.php/moenia/article/view/6474
